source: Jacobson et al., Analysis of the Xedni Calculus Attack (2000), section 3.2 Steps 1-7 and Remark 1

base_curve.ordered_pair_law: all distinct nonidentity E(F_47) point pairs

lift_rule.a4_a6_rule: for each integer a2, solve the two lifted point equations uniquely when x1 differs from x2

auxiliary_gates.common: x coordinates distinct modulo each auxiliary prime, integral coefficients, good reduction and rank-two Weierstrass incidence rows

coefficient_policy.search: enumerate a2 residues modulo 7 and 11 satisfying their curve-order gate; combine with a2=0 mod 47 by CRT
coefficient_policy.arm_priority: strict order 6 at 11 first, then weak order 7
coefficient_policy.choice: within an arm sort candidate centered CRT representatives by (abs(a2),a2), take the first nonsingular rational curve

relation.rational_event: Q1+2*Q2=O over Q on the chosen curve

run_cap: complete finite census with all failed and accepted pair rows; no wall-time performance inference
interpretation: Deterministic r=2 CRT curve choice within one three-parameter Weierstrass family; no multi-prime point CRT or discriminant optimization
